_comment: Release manifest. Every Hub with update checks on fetches this file and compares its own version against `version`. Bump it as part of cutting a release, not before - the harness pins it equal to package.json so a manifest that lies about the current release cannot ship.
notes: 2.37.0: a Logbook for every printer - what went wrong, what fixed it, and a maintenance schedule by print hours or days. Pauses and errors the printer reports, and printers you take out of service, are logged by themselves; what's due shows on the printer card and can ping your phone. 2.36.0: the planner stops leaving printers idle - no more waiting until midnight for a job to 'fit', and running prints no longer draw twice on the timeline. Models: format folders like U1 and prusa-format are no longer treated as designers, Random shows every model before repeating one and mixes designers, and Rename/Attributes/Delete moved behind a corner menu. Fixed: pressing Open in Orca could freeze the whole Hub for up to half an hour on a network share. 2.35.0: fixes the freeze reported in issue #4 - with several cameras streaming, the page could stop updating after a few minutes; a tile now asks for one frame at a time and the Hub grabs a printer's frame once for everyone waiting. On screens 1500px and wider the dashboard, Dispatch, Models and Match views use the room, so four U1s fit in one row on a 4K monitor. 2.34.0: timelapses are now actually captured, not just fetched. The 2.27-2.33 pipeline assumed each printer's firmware renders its own finished timelapse and just grabbed the file - checked the whole fleet and that hasn't produced anything new since January, on any printer. This rebuilds it as originally planned: the Hub watches each print's layer count and grabs a frame from the chamber camera every time it advances, then assembles the frames into the video itself with ffmpeg when the print finishes - the logo intro and photo outro from 2.32/2.33 composite onto that the same as before. A Hub restart mid-print picks capture back up from wherever the print currently is. 2.33.0: sort the Models tab - designer, name, newest, oldest, random, or most printed. Most printed counts completed jobs from your printers' own history against the files they were sliced from, and says how many it matched. 2.32.1: fixes 2.32's video compositing - it was applying frame rate twice (once in the filter, once as a separate ffmpeg flag), which visibly scrambled the timelapse footage into a corrupted mess. Removed the redundant flag; the compositing itself (logo intro + photo outro) is unchanged. 2.32: timelapses now fade out to a photo of the finished print instead of carrying a burned-in 'Shop link in bio' graphic - that text is gone for good; real Shop links will come from TikTok's own native product tagging once the Shop is live. Drop a logo file at sf3dTimelapse.logoFile in config.json and every new video will also fade in from it at the start - no code change needed. 2.31: TikTok posting - a finished print's timelapse gets queued to post, gated on the same publish_social flag that already keeps sold-at-shows-only items off the website. 2.30.2: fixes the phone - since 2.29 the page could be wider than the screen and the printer cards were cut off at the right edge. 2.30.1: an Export CSV button on the What sells table. 2.30: tidy the shelf from the shelf - Rename files a model as Designer\\Name\\Designer - Name.3mf (it shows you where first, never over an existing file), Attributes fixes a designer or name the folders got wrong and offers the same move, Delete removes a file for good after one confirm. 2.29: what it actually sells for - type a piece's real price beside the worth-printing line and get the plate's take, dollars per printer hour, dollars per gram and margin over filament as you type; Save keeps a row per file and the table lists every priced file, most profitable per printer hour first. 2.28.1: a readability pass on the dark look - brighter text at every level, bigger type (nothing under 10.5px), panels that lift off the background, edges you can see. Same identity, same accent. 2.28: slicer settings from the file - on a Models card, Settings has Claude look at the plate render inside the 3MF, numbers the Hub measures from the meshes (size, overhangs, floating undersides, bed contact, painted faces, volume) and the designer's own profile, then suggest the settings to set in Orca for the printer you pick; same key as the pre-flight, nothing sent until you press it, a few cents each. Worth printing: one line under the selected file with what its filament costs, the least it has to sell for (per piece when the name carries the plate count, like Penguin x20.gcode) and what that is per printer hour, from two rates in Settings. Fixed: the AI pre-flight button on the job card did nothing since 2.25. 2.27: SF3D timelapse uploads - no capture code, no chamber-camera websocket. Each U1 already renders its own finished timelapse in firmware; this listens for a print finishing, grabs the file the printer already made, and hands it to the SF3D storefront. 2.26: a Models tab for the 3MF files you have not sliced yet - designer folders, the plate render and painted colors from inside each file, and an Open in Orca button that watches for the gcode you save (desktop only). 2.25: AI pre-flight on the job card - with your own Anthropic key, Claude reads the slicer settings in the file and compares them with what is loaded in the printer you picked; GO, CHECK or STOP and why. Nothing is sent until you press the button, never the gcode itself, about a cent a review. 2.24: import your rolls from Spoolman (one way, re-import any time); push notifications to your phone through ntfy when a print finishes, pauses with the reason, errors, or a printer stops answering; rolls count down by themselves when a print finishes, with cost per print and an Undo; wildcards in the library filter; the QR scan button says why it is off on plain http.
